title: Industry Norms and the Worker's Perspective

sections.content:
You know third-person plural impersonals and indefinite *uno* from B2 Unit 21. In discussions of labour markets and working conditions, these two impersonal forms divide what 'employers or the sector' do from what 'a worker' experiences.

A subjectless third-person plural verb refers to unnamed employers, recruiters or institutions and excludes the speaker: *En este sector remuneran las horas extra aparte*, *En muchas compañías recurren a la subcontratación*. It states a prevailing industry practice without naming a specific company.

Indefinite *uno* (or *una* when a woman speaks of herself as a typical worker) brings the speaker inside the generalisation: *Cuando uno trabaja por cuenta propia, paga sus propias prestaciones*, *Con la antigüedad, una valora más la estabilidad*. Every verb, reflexive pronoun (*se*) and possessive (*su*) linked to *uno / una* stays in the third person singular.

sections.title: Employer/sector practice vs. worker's experience
rows: En esa industria suelen exigir disponibilidad total.
Si te despiden sin causa, deben pagarte la indemnización.
Cuando uno trabaja por cuenta propia, asume su propio riesgo.
Cuando una entra en nómina, gana seguridad en sus prestaciones.

items.spanish: En muchas consultoras pagan una parte en nómina y otra por objetivos.
items.english: In many consultancies they pay one part on the payroll and another by targets.

items.spanish: A veces despiden personal durante una crisis y luego recurren a la subcontratación.
items.english: Sometimes they lay off staff during a crisis and then resort to outsourcing.

items.spanish: Cuando uno trabaja por cuenta propia, organiza su horario pero cubre sus prestaciones.
items.english: When you work self-employed, you organise your schedule but cover your own benefits.

items.spanish: Con los años de antigüedad, una aprende a negociar mejor su salario.
items.english: With years of seniority, you (a woman speaking) learn to negotiate your salary better.

sections.content: English uses generic *you* for both *When you work freelance...* and *They pay well in that sector*. In formal Spanish, do not mix *uno* with second-person *tu* or *te*: write *Cuando uno pierde su empleo, se preocupa*, never *Cuando uno pierde tu empleo*. Use the third-person plural when talking about what unnamed employers do, and *uno / una* when putting yourself in the worker's shoes.
